title: Sell Mineral Rights in Negley, OH
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Negley, OH | Columbiana County
metaDescription: Negley sits in Columbiana County's Utica flank near the Pennsylvania line. See how border-county position affects a mineral rights sale here.
heroLead: Negley is a small community in Columbiana County near the Pennsylvania state line, on the northern flank of the Utica/Point Pleasant play, where drilling activity has been lighter and more selective than in Ohio's core counties further south.
intro: Being close to the state line means Negley-area mineral owners sometimes hear about Pennsylvania Marcellus activity from neighbors just across the border, but Ohio and Pennsylvania run different regulatory systems, and Columbiana County's own Utica flank position is what actually drives value here.

sections.heading: Border-county geology and why it's treated conservatively
paragraphs: Columbiana County's flank position means the Utica/Point Pleasant formation here is thinner and less consistently productive than in core counties like Carroll or Belmont. That doesn't rule out value, but a buyer will lean on the closest available well and permit data before pricing a Negley-area interest.

sections.heading: Why Pennsylvania activity doesn't set the local price
paragraphs: Pennsylvania's Marcellus shale leasing and royalty structures operate under different state law than Ohio, so lease terms or bonus figures heard about from across the border in Pennsylvania don't directly apply to Ohio-side acreage near Negley. Value here should be benchmarked against Columbiana County and nearby Ohio counties.

sections.heading: Recorder records in Lisbon
paragraphs: The Columbiana County Recorder's office, located in the county seat of Lisbon, holds deed and lease records covering Negley. A title check there will confirm whether your interest has ever been leased and whether it was formally severed from the surface.

faqs.question: Does Negley's proximity to Pennsylvania affect its mineral rights value?
faqs.answer: Not directly. Pennsylvania and Ohio have separate oil and gas laws, so Marcellus lease terms across the border don't set the price for Ohio-side acreage. Local Columbiana County activity is what matters.

faqs.question: Is Columbiana County part of the Utica core?
faqs.answer: No, it's generally flank territory, thinner and less consistently drilled than core counties like Carroll and Belmont to the south.

faqs.question: Where are records kept for Negley-area mineral rights?
faqs.answer: The Columbiana County Recorder's office in Lisbon holds deed and lease records for the entire county, including Negley.

faqs.question: What if I've never received any lease offer for my Negley property?
faqs.answer: That's common for flank-position land this far north. It doesn't mean the interest has no value, only that a buyer will price it more conservatively based on the nearest active units rather than existing income.

faqs.question: Does the state line create any confusion for royalty tax reporting?
faqs.answer: Only in the sense that owners sometimes mix up which state's rules apply. Ohio-source royalty income from a Negley-area well is reported under Ohio and federal rules regardless of where you personally live, so keep your statements organized by well and by year.
